instantiated_cells.justification: The statute defines a "lobbyist" as any individual employed by a principal or who contracts for/receives economic consideration (other than reimbursement of actual expenses) from a principal whose duties include lobbying — no dollar floor on compensation is set.
The lobbyist definition is based on receiving economic consideration to lobby, not on any expenditure threshold by the lobbyist; no lobbyist-side spending trigger exists in the statute.

A principal must register only after expenditures/obligations for non-exempt lobbying exceed $500 in a calendar year, and a principal anticipating not exceeding $500 may file a verified statement exempting it from licensing, registration, and reporting requirements.

unscoreable_emissions.reason: The Wisconsin statute contains no percent-of-compensated-time de minimis exemption for lobbyist filing. §13.68(1)(a) excludes time of non-lobbyist employees who devote not more than 10 hours to lobbying in a reporting period from principal expense reporting, but that is an absolute hours figure (not a percentage) and applies to non-lobbyist employees, not to the lobbyist's own filing duty. No percentage threshold exists in the bundled text.

content.text:
I'll analyze each cell against the Wisconsin statute text.

**Row 001**: §13.62(11) defines "lobbyist" as one who receives economic consideration "other than reimbursement for actual expenses" — so anyone paid any amount qualifies (no dollar threshold). This is a YES/0 threshold.

**Row 002**: No expenditure threshold on the lobbyist themselves to trigger lobbyist status — the definition is based on receiving compensation, not on spending.

**Row 003**: §13.62(11) — if duties are not exclusively lobbying, the individual is a lobbyist only if making lobbying communications on at least 5 days within a reporting period.

**Row 004**: §13.68(1)(a)5 — expenditures for paid advertising/grassroots only reported if exceeding $500; §13.68(1)(a)6 — lobbyist itemization only if exceeding $200. Not all expenses required.

**Row 005**: §13.621(5) and §13.64(1) — $500 aggregate threshold; principals under $500 exempt from registration/reporting.

**Row 006**: §13.68(1)(a) excludes from required reporting any non-lobbyist employee who devotes not more than 10 hours to lobbying in a reporting period — this is hours, not a percentage. No percent-of-compensated-time exemption exists in the statute.

input.justification: The statute defines a "lobbyist" as any individual employed by a principal or who contracts for/receives economic consideration (other than reimbursement of actual expenses) from a principal whose duties include lobbying — no dollar floor on compensation is set.
The lobbyist definition is based on receiving economic consideration to lobby, not on any expenditure threshold by the lobbyist; no lobbyist-side spending trigger exists in the statute.
If an individual's duties are not exclusively lobbying, the person is a lobbyist only if he or she makes lobbying communications on each of at least 5 days within a reporting period.

Paid advertising/grassroots lobbying expenditures are reported only if they exceed $500 in the reporting period, and per-lobbyist itemization is required only when lobbying expenditures to that lobbyist exceed $200 — so not all individual expenditures must be disclosed.

A principal must register only after expenditures/obligations for non-exempt lobbying exceed $500 in a calendar year, and a principal anticipating not exceeding $500 may file a verified statement exempting it from licensing, registration, and reporting requirements.

No percentage threshold exists in the bundled text.
